title: Machine Learning Time Series Forecasting: A Comprehensive Survey and Stock Market Application
tldr: Comprehensive survey identifies LightGBM and LSTM as top-performing time series models, with day trading application achieving 20,000 bps daily returns.
problem_and_motivation: Time series prediction faces challenges from complex factors including countless individuals and institutions acting simultaneously. Existing surveys struggle to draw meaningful comparisons because they analyze independent studies with different implementations and datasets. There is a need for systematic comparison within uniform experimental frameworks.
approach: Conducted systematic survey of 79 papers comparing tree-based ML and deep learning methods.
Focused on studies with identical experimental setups for apples-to-apples comparison.
Developed day trading model using LightGBM with engineered features from second-by-second data.
Applied two years of trade and quote data from all U.S. equities for model training.
Evaluated models using realistic execution constraints and simulated trading performance.
findings: num: LightGBM and LSTM consistently outperform other alternatives in time series forecasting.
num: Tree-based methods demonstrate significant advantage in computational efficiency.
num: Data quality is most influential factor overshadowing hyperparameter tuning benefits.
num: Day trading model achieves 20,000 bps average daily profit with Sharpe ratio of 15.78.
num: Model performance exceeds top human day traders by more than 500 times.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This thesis provides a comprehensive survey of ML methods for time series prediction within uniform experimental frameworks. It identifies LightGBM and LSTM as consistently top-performing architectures across diverse forecasting tasks. The work demonstrates practical application through a day trading model achieving exceptional returns. Findings emphasize data quality importance and computational efficiency advantages of tree-based methods.
directly_justifies: LightGBM and LSTM consistently outperform other methods in comparative studies.
Data quality is most influential factor affecting model performance.
Day trading model achieves 20,000 bps daily profit exceeding human traders by 500x.
Tree-based methods offer significant computational efficiency advantages.
Combining models and diverse information sources boosts forecasting performance.
limits: Survey limited to papers comparing TBML and DL methods within same experimental setup.
Day trading model evaluated only on U.S. equities market data.
Performance metrics may not account for all real-world trading constraints.
Computational costs of large-scale model training not fully quantified.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan of all topic domains identified high relevance for predictive modeling (6.A) and forecasting algorithms (6.B) due to core focus on ML methods for financial time series. Medium relevance for landscape of existing systems (4.A), ML model serving (14.B), and algorithmic evaluation (12.B) as supporting aspects. Domains related to Filipino demographics, budgeting strategies, anomaly detection, and mobile design were considered and rejected as not covered by this ML forecasting survey and application paper.
